speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with a headache and worsening vision over three weeks; to begin our evaluation, can you describe the specific nature and location of your headache, and do you notice any visual changes like blurriness, double vision, or loss of peripheral vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis)

Given your age of 69 and the classic triad of new headache, worsening vision, and the absence of systemic symptoms like fever or weight loss, I suspect vasculitis of the temporal arteries. Could you confirm if you have experienced jaw pain while chewing (jaw claudication) or any scalp tenderness? Also, have you noticed any vision loss in one eye specifically?
